content: PostgreSQL sequences guarantee uniqueness + concurrency but are never gapless: nextval is not rolled back, so aborted transactions/crashes leave holes; also sequence numbers jump backwards after crash recovery (cybertec). For gapless document numbers (invoices, business docs): counter table locked FOR UPDATE (or UPDATE ... RETURNING singleton row) serializes number allocation per granularity (per country/month/type), guaranteed ascending+gapless but serialize those transactions — keep them short. Professional guidance: 'think twice before building a gapless sequence — it serializes all transactions using it' — only worth it for legally significant numbers (Indonesian BAST numbers qualify as business documents where gaps look wrong to auditors). Alternative per-type sequences if gaps acceptable.
